title: Marketplace images, custom images and the Compute Gallery

videos.script: Every virtual machine starts from an image, and most people never look at one. This lesson does. {{source}} An image is not something a machine boots from. Azure copies it into a new disk, and the machine boots from the copy. There are three kinds of image, and the lesson names each one. {{urn}} Then the Marketplace. An image there has four names, joined by colons. You will read the list the command line carries with it, and find out why Ubuntu 24.04 is missing from it. {{latest}} The last of the four names is usually latest. That is not a version. It is a question Azure answers on the day the machine is created. {{own}} Next, an image of your own. You configure a machine, clean it, and capture it. Or you skip the image and hand a stock machine a cloud-init file at first boot. You will compile both. {{gallery}} Last, the Compute Gallery. A gallery holds definitions, and a definition holds numbered versions. You decide which version counts as latest, where its copies live, and who may use it.
